claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing revenue, Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion, and AWS's AI and custom-silicon businesses each passed a $25 billion annualized run rate.
Gartner says by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report says cloud value from innovation is worth 5x more than cost savings and EBITDA uplift of 20–30% by 2030 for high performers.
AWS posted $42.2 billion revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter, its fastest growth since 2021.
AWS's AI business and chips business (including Trainium and Graviton) each exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time; Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year in fiscal Q4 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said 'This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time.'
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026, and its backlog reached $514 billion, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195–205 billion, up from $180–190 billion that had already been raised twice this year.

Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39%, with remaining performance obligations of $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals totaling $75 billion.
Hybrid cloud will grow from $130B to $310–330B by 2030 per ResearchAndMarkets.
87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds per Mordor Intelligence.
Gartner predicts 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers found 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure.
Gartner forecasts total worldwide AI spending to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027 half of enterprises will be using AI agents.
Gartner predicts by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms, with spending on securing AI reaching roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
Carlie Idoine, VP Analyst at Gartner, said at the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in Sydney that AI needs to be tightly aligned with data, analytics, and governance.
Gartner predicts by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations have a dedicated platform engineering team and 35% run a hybrid platform combining developer platforms with AI tooling.
Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said developers are standardizing on CNCF projects and organizations are extending platforms to support AI workloads.
Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029, while human-in-the-loop requirements fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.

Pulumi's 2026 survey found 82% agree AI agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months, 63% say they trust agents to make production changes while manual approval remains close to universal, and expectation of agents generating half or more of code rises from 45% to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails.
Mordor Intelligence says the global Kubernetes market is USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.

CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%, and 30% of backend developers using Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, attributed to maturity.
Gartner says by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use them.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a generally available MCP server for its Agent Toolkit.
Mirantis's Lens launched a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.
Pulumi Agent Skills work with Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI to reduce hallucination for Pulumi projects.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
The 2026 predictions from last year's edition held up.
The 2027 edition covers 10 trends.
